title: Synkrisis: a browser-based tool for the comparative evaluation of translation versions
description: Synkrisis is a self-contained, browser-based tool for the comparative evaluation of translation versions (human and machine translations, retranslations) within the same language: segmentation, alignment and collation against a base text, with descriptive annotation based on an adapted subset of van Leuven-Zwart's model of translation shifts and evaluative annotation based on selected MQM error dimensions, without scoring. Texts are processed locally in the browser and are not stored. Includes an annotated example session (Alphonse Daudet, 'La mule du Pape', five machine translation outputs into Greek). Developed by Eleni Tziafa, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens. Designed and implemented in collaboration with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic). Live version: https://elenitziafa.com/synkrisis.html
